title: Compactness: finite satisfiability and infinite models
summary: Finite satisfiability gives a common model; size requirements produce infinite models and show why finitude cannot be axiomatized.
abstract: Requiring at least one element, at least two, and so on passes every finite test in a finite set, but satisfying all these requirements takes an infinite domain. The compactness theorem shows that any collection of first-order requirements in a countable language has a model if each finite subcollection has one. It follows that a theory with arbitrarily large finite models must also have an infinite model. First-order sentences can specify a particular finite size or require infinitude through infinitely many axioms, but no theory describes all and only the finite structures. The proofs also show how a theory can have a model containing an object that none of its closed terms names.

based_on.title: Sets, Logic, Computation
